content:
Reports indicate that Apple is piloting a new "Live Notes" system at some of its retail stores. According to the latest report, the system uses artificial intelligence to record and transcribe conversations between "Genius Bar" staff and customers.

Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman pointed out in the latest issue of his "Power On" newsletter that the Live Notes system allows Apple Store employees to "use AI tools to record conversations, and transcribe and summarise their interactions with customers".

The relevant transcripts are subsequently stored in Apple's internal Genius Bar system. According to Bloomberg, the move aims to allow employees to focus on customer service without the distraction of taking notes.

Reports say that using Live Notes requires consent from both the employee and the customer before conversations during Genius Bar service can be recorded.

Nevertheless, Apple retail employees are reportedly concerned about how the Live Notes system might be used in the future:

Currently, Live Notes is not mandatory. Bloomberg said it is unclear whether Apple will extend the system to more stores, make it mandatory, or change how the transcripts are used.
